title: Improve tool-calling execution ergonomics: multi-tool/parallel calls, result injection, retries
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: customers building multi-step tool workflows need ergonomics for invoking multiple tools per turn, running tools in parallel, reliably injecting tool results back into the model context, and transparent retry semantics. This PR implements API and runtime changes to support: 1) explicit multi-tool invocation in a single assistant turn with deterministic ordering and optional parallel execution hints, 2) a new tool_result injection API that appends sanitized tool outputs to the model input while preserving structured metadata for observability, 3) idempotent tool call IDs and retry-first semantics so SDKs and servers can safely retry transient failures without double-calling side-effecting tools, 4) streaming stability improvements to ensure tool outputs can be streamed and merged into the assistant stream without interleaving corruption, and 5) OpenAI-compat layer updates so that existing tool-calling clients see compatible shapes and backwards-compatible fallbacks. Changes include API surface additions, runtime scheduler improvements, KV/prefix cache adaptations, SDK helpers, and detailed tests and migration notes. Checklist: Implement core API and runtime, add SDK helpers (python/ts), update OpenAI-compat adapter, add unit/integration tests, update docs and release notes, add migration guide. Migration notes: Default behavior is backwards-compatible. Consumers opt into parallel execution via flags. Tool authors should adopt idempotent call IDs when invoking side-effecting tools; SDKs will auto-generate stable IDs unless the client supplies one. Observability: tool_call_id and tool_result_key are emitted as tags on traces and metrics. Testing: added integration test harness that simulates flakey tool endpoints and verifies single-call semantics under retries.

release_notes: Tool-calling: add support for multi-tool invocations in a single assistant turn
Tool-calling: opt-in parallel execution hints for lower end-to-end latency
Tool-calling: idempotent tool_call_id to enable safe retries and at-most-once semantics for side-effecting tools
API: tool_result injection that appends sanitized tool outputs to model input with structured metadata
OpenAI-compat: adapter updated to maintain backwards compatibility while exposing new ergonomics
SDK: python/typescript helpers for tool-call ids and parsing tool_result metadata
notes_for_ops: Operators: scheduler gains new config knobs 'max_parallel_tool_calls' and 'tool_call_retry_window_ms'. Default values are conservative and zero-config compatible. Rolling restart required for runtime nodes to pick up scheduler changes when deploying to Dedicated/Private clusters. Monitor trace tag 'tool_call_id' to correlate calls with downstream tool metrics.
documentation_updates: docs/tool-calling.md updated with examples for multi-tool calls, parallel hints, idempotency guidance, and migration steps. OpenAI-compat docs include a compatibility table and example payloads. SDK CHANGELOGs updated.
testing_summary: Added unit tests for stream merging, idempotency, and tool result injection. Integration tests simulate flaky external tool endpoints and verify single-call semantics under retries and parallel execution. CI matrix includes python/ts integration runs.
